MARKET.head: Texas High Plains growers struggle as pandemic wine boom ends, contracts fade
MARKET.summ: As Texas wines earn broader recognition, the High Plains growers behind much of that progress are navigating a market correction that could shape the state’s next chapter
takeaways: Texas wine industry relies on 644-kilometre separation between High Plains growers and Hill Country wineries, a system built on handshake trust now under strain.
Pandemic surge from 2020 to early 2023 drove aggressive grape purchases and rising prices; when consumer sales softened, inventories backed up and buyers withdrew.
Growers now farm by contract tier: fully contracted blocks receive premium care; uncontracted fruit gets minimal attention to preserve cash, directly linking vineyard investment to buyer certainty.
March 2025 freeze lowered High Plains yields significantly, particularly whites, creating a painful reset that may rebalance supply but threatens growers already facing multi-year losses.
Major growers including Jet Wilmeth, Andy Timmons and Neal Newsom are retiring or reducing acreage, forcing wineries dependent on their fruit to confront succession risk and regional fragility.

MARKET.head: Anheuser-Busch becomes top wine seller via BeatBox acquisition
MARKET.summ: A lot of people lost their minds in the ’80s. Compared to the decade’s cocaine-addled and clinically insane, August Busch III, the legendary head honcho at the macrobrewer that bore his name, stayed very much in control. But even the steely “Three Sticks” was not totally immune to the siren song of flash-in-the-pan fads, slick...
takeaways: Anheuser-Busch InBev acquired an 85-percent stake in BeatBox, the wine-based beverage brand, for $490 million in February 2026, with a path to full ownership.
BeatBox's performance under ABI ownership reversed the brewer's poor track record in wine, which included discontinued brands Dewey Stevens (1986) and Babe Wine (2023).
BeatBox alone propelled ABI to sixth among all wine marketers with seven million cases in 2025, accounting for roughly 40 percent of the wine-based cocktails category.
BeatBox grew around 30 percent in dollars and volume in the 52 weeks through mid-April 2026, with its Cherry Limeade flavor outselling Bud Light Lime-a-Rita in dollars.
Wine-based cocktails surged to 18 million cases in 2025, led by BeatBox and competitor BuzzBallz Chillers, offsetting broader wine category declines.

MARKET.head: English estates launch prestige cuvées to rival Champagne's finest
MARKET.summ: Are English prestige cuvées worth prices that rival the top end of Champagne?
takeaways: Nyetimber released England's first prestige cuvée in 2018, the 1086 white and rosé at £150-£175, modelled on Champagne's concept after proprietor Eric Heerema acquired the estate in 2006.

Chapel Down's Kit's Coty Coeur de Cuvée (2013 vintage debut, now £126) and Gusbourne's Fifty One Degrees North (2022 debut at £195, magnum at £395) joined the super-premium sparkling market with seven to eight years lees ageing.

Langham created a solera-based Perpetual Blanc de Blancs released in 2025 at £109.95, blending grapes from 2017-2020 vintages in a single 2,000L oak foudre to express Chardonnay across multiple years.

Squerryes launched Patience 2014 in July 2026, its prestige cuvée from a family-owned Kent estate on North Downs chalk, named after a 17th-century merchant ancestor and released nearly a decade after preserving the vintage.

MARKET.head: Centre-Loire appellations gain traction as Sancerre prices soar past fifty dollars
MARKET.summ: Those interested in French wine are undoubtedly familiar with the Loire Valley, but digging a little deeper, there are many subregions within this expansive viticultural area to get to know. One of them is the Centre-Loire. And although the slightly misleading name suggests it’s the center of France’s lengthy and endlessly...
takeaways: Sancerre Sauvignon Blanc now sells for $40 to $50 per bottle, forcing buyers toward cheaper neighboring appellations: Pouilly-Fumé, Menetou-Salon, Quincy, Reuilly, and Coteaux du Giennois, most priced $20 to $30.
Clément Berthier, Sancerre appellation president, states the region is at production capacity with no plans to expand vineyards or output, limiting supply growth.

Centre-Loire producers report rising harvest dates driven by climate change, with 2024 picking potentially beginning August 20, forcing winegrowers to experiment with abandoned acidic varieties to preserve freshness.
Paul-Henry Pellé, organic farmer at Domaine Pellé in Menetou-Salon, and Emile Balland in Coteaux du Giennois both cite acidity loss as the primary challenge from warming temperatures.
Nearly three-quarters of Sancerre production is exported, with half reaching the United States, while neighboring appellation exports remain much smaller despite rising quality and availability.

MARKET.head: Celebrity wine launches surge from 2005 to 2025, with 2020 peak
MARKET.summ: The alcohol industry has seen an influx of celebrity-owned brands in recent decades, and the wine category is not immune to the trend. Whether birthed from genuine wine connoisseurship or just a marketing ploy, celebrity wine brands now make up a considerable sector of the industry. Famous people amass dedicated followers, and...
takeaways: Kyle MacLachlan, actor in Twin Peaks, launched Pursued by Bear winery in Walla Walla in 2005, marking an early entry by a major celebrity into wine production.
A wave of celebrity wine brands accelerated sharply in 2020, with Post Malone, Cameron Diaz, Snoop Dogg, and Mary J. Blige all debuting labels that year during pandemic lockdowns.
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie's Château Miraval in Provence, purchased in 2012 and launched commercially in 2013, became entangled in their divorce; Pitt now owns 50 percent of the estate.
Celebrity wine brands now represent a considerable sector of the wine industry, leveraging famous founders' fanbases to drive sales of rosés, sparkling wines, and organic offerings.
Most celebrity labels emphasize specific styles or production methods: organic viticulture (Avaline), low-intervention winemaking (MianU), or French rosé blends (Maison No. 9, Hampton Water).

MARKET.head: Soju surges past shōchū in U.S. market as Asian spirits gain share
MARKET.summ: As consumer interest grows, soju, shōchū, and baijiu are following distinct paths in the U.S. market, signaling that Asian spirits are evolving beyond a single trend
takeaways: Soju grew 133 percent between 2019 and 2025 to under one percent of U.S. spirits volume, while shōchū rose only 11 percent over the same period, according to IWSR consulting director Koryn Ternes.

Green bottle soju, the mass-produced sweet style made mandatory by Korea's 1965 rice ban, dominates U.S. exports and retail shelves, with Jinro the world's best-selling spirit for 25 consecutive years.

James Barlow, fine wine and Asia portfolio manager at Spec's in Texas, said the retailer purchased under $1 million in Asian spirits in 2018 but now buys multi-millions, crediting soju's fruity flavors and lower ABV.
Craft soju producers like Tokki Soju, founded in Brooklyn in 2016 by Douglas Park, are slowly gaining ground as consumers mature beyond green bottle brands and seek traditional expressions.
Shōchū brands iichiko and Mizu focus on bars and restaurants rather than retail, with higher-proof cocktail-ready options targeting bartenders as key ambassadors to reach whisky and mezcal drinkers.

MARKET.head: RNDC files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after shedding majority of markets
MARKET.summ: Republic National Distributing Company (RNDC), formerly the second-largest wine and spirits distributor in the United States, has filed for bankruptcy after a yearlong shakedown. The distributor voluntarily filed for chapter 11 yesterday in the Southern District of Texas to initiate a court-facilitated process of shuttering the...
takeaways: Republic National Distributing Company, formerly the second-largest US wine and spirits distributor, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Texas yesterday to wind down remaining operations and seek buyers.
RNDC lists liabilities of $1–10 billion against assets of $500 million, $1 billion, with over 100,000 creditors and $300 million in unsecured claims led by $93.92 million owed to Proximo Spirits.

The distributor sold off majority of its markets in recent months to Reyes Beverage Group, Columbia Distributing, Martignetti Companies, and BreakThru Beverage Group after exiting California last June.
Bankruptcy does not include National Distributing Company or RNDC's six joint ventures in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and New York, though the Alaska joint venture is included.
Small suppliers face potential losses as they lack leverage to demand payment upfront; approximately 1,450 remaining employees will continue to receive wages under a court-approved first day motion.

CULTURE.head: Penn Station bottle shop stocks niche wines for commuters and tristate demand
CULTURE.summ: It’d be an understatement to say that no one enjoys Penn Station. When most New Yorkers and out-of-towners trek through the sterilely lit and highly trafficked train station, they have one goal in mind: Get in, and get out. But if there’s one reprieve for travelers slugging their suitcases through the Midtown terminal, it’s Penn Cellars.
takeaways: Penn Cellars, opened late December 2024 in Penn Station's transit hub, stocks niche producers from Josh Cellars to Frank Cornelissen alongside mass-market bottles.
Buyer David Bruno, formerly in fine dining, pitches unfamiliar wines to commuters and has shifted many toward higher-quality choices at lower price points.
The station's foot traffic draws Tri-State travelers who request small-allocation wines unavailable in suburban retail, creating demand for cult bottles outside New York City.
Ready-to-drink canned and boxed wines drive sales to commuters boarding evening trains, with Bruno offering plastic cups and ice for immediate consumption.
Tracks bar, reopening in Penn Station under original owner Bruce Caulfield, will collaborate with Penn Cellars to expand wine education and on-premise sales.

CULTURE.head: Ancient vine-training systems vanish as labor costs and mechanization reshape European viticulture
CULTURE.summ: As labor costs soar, global wine regions are forced to weigh the high expense of traditional vineyard design against its tourism appeal and climate-adapting benefits
takeaways: Italy's alberata system, once common around Naples, survives on only a handful of hectares after being replaced by mechanizable methods like Guyot and vertical shoot positioning.

Lanzarote's hoyo pits, dug after volcanic eruptions in 1730-1736, remain viable because tourism draws thousands of visitors; active vineyards fell 19 percent between 2000 and 2026 despite local subsidies.
Rías Baixas producers maintain the labor-intensive pergola for Albariño because specialized machinery now handles ground tasks, and the DO bans mechanized harvest anyway.

Veneto's bellussera hybrid, which once supported silk production and livestock, fell from common practice to nine percent of Piave DOC as those industries vanished; climate resilience and wine tourism may revive it.
Survival of traditional systems depends on region-specific economics: tourism, local regulation, mechanization aids, and climate adaptation determine whether heritage vineyards thrive or disappear.

CULTURE.head: Brooklyn housing complex installs pathways from 450,000 recycled wine corks
CULTURE.summ: Wine bottle corks are getting a second lease on life in New York City. Earlier this month, a New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) project in Brooklyn cut the ribbon on newly paved pathways and playground surfaces made of upcycled corks. The first-of-its-kind installation is part of the nonprofit Public Housing Community...
takeaways: Public Housing Community Fund, Cork Collective, and nonprofits built playgrounds and walkways from 450,000 wine bottle corks at Marlboro Houses in Gravesend, Brooklyn.
Cork Collective, founded by architecture firm Rockwell Group and cork maker Amorim in 2024, sourced corks from NYC restaurants, ground them, and mixed with adhesive before laying.
Children at Marlboro Houses submitted playground designs that shaped the final installation, making the project resident-led.
Cork surfaces absorb stormwater to reduce flooding, contain no toxic materials unlike plastic or asphalt, and lower ambient temperature by 20 to 30 percent.
Fewer than one percent of 13 billion corks made annually are recycled; three billion are discarded yearly in the US.

CULTURE.head: Independent wine merchant wins inaugural sustainable buyer award
CULTURE.summ: The London Wine Fair revealed the winners of its Drinks Buyers Awards at the event’s recent 45th edition. For the second year running, Decanter sponsored the Sustainable Drinks Buyer of the Year category
takeaways: Di Camillo, owner of Wine & Such, won Decanter's first Sustainable Wine Buyer award for embedding sustainability throughout sourcing and shop operations.
The judging panel found her entry stood out for weaving sustainability into every decision rather than adopting isolated initiatives like cork recycling.
Majestic won the separate Sustainable Drinks Buying Team of the Year award in the same inaugural competition.
A significant number of entrants left the sustainability section blank, suggesting many buyers either overlook or undervalue the criterion.
The Wine Buyers Awards, launched in 2020, added the sustainability category in 2025 to recognise buyers shaping industry trends toward responsible practices.

SCIENCE.head: Disease-resistant grape hybrids cut fungicide sprays 80 percent, gain European plantings
SCIENCE.summ: Fungus-resistant hybrid grape varieties, known as PIWIs, are evolving through advances in breeding, offering growers new options in a changing climate
takeaways: PIWIs, or fungus-resistant hybrid grapes, require two to three fungicide sprays per season versus eight to 15 for traditional varieties, reducing chemical, fuel, and labor costs.

Modern genetic testing technology rhAmpSeq, deployed since 2019 via the US VitisGen initiative, lets breeders identify disease-resistance genes with precision and stack multiple protective layers into single varieties.

German plantings reached 4,000 hectares in 2025, up 10 percent annually; France is developing ResDur hybrids crossed with Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot to maintain regional signature while resisting mildew.
A 2026 Luxembourg study found PIWIs delivered twofold economic savings and threefold environmental benefit over traditional varieties, with largest gains in soil health and reduced water toxicity.

PIWIs require no change to existing vineyard practices beyond reduced spraying; industry success depends on tasting mature-vine commercial volumes and competitive retail pricing alongside sustainability messaging.

SCIENCE.head: Vineyards deploy netting to cool fruit clusters amid heat stress
SCIENCE.summ: Netting is no longer just for hail, it is becoming one of viticulture's most versatile climate adaptation tools
takeaways: Vineyard netting, traditionally used for hail and bird protection, is now being engineered to reduce cluster temperature and preserve color, acidity, and phenolics during heat events.
UC Davis research on Cabernet Sauvignon showed shaded clusters retained 27 percent more anthocyanins than unshaded fruit when temperatures exceeded the 35-degree Celsius degradation threshold.

At Catena Zapata in Mendoza, light netting intercepts roughly 15 percent of radiation; Luis Reginato, head of viticulture, observes reduced vine stress in hot conditions without blocking beneficial UV exposure.

At Petra in Tuscany, Marco Simonit's 2025 trials found white and green shade nets more effective than black nets; Merlot sunburn dropped from 41 percent in unshaded control to three percent under 90 percent shade.

At Boroli in Barolo, netting placement matters critically: fabric must be kept away from clusters to avoid heat burn, and open nets outperformed dense ones, suggesting shade level and airflow balance the benefits against heat trapping.

SCIENCE.head: Grape sunburn spreads beyond hot regions as heat waves shift vineyard practices
SCIENCE.summ: As climate change makes heat waves more prevalent, more producers have to combat sunburn in grapes, and the flabby, flat, rubbery notes they can bring to wine
takeaways: Sunburn occurs when berry surface temperature exceeds 104–109°F under high light, causing chlorophyll and polyphenols to degrade and producing flavors of asphalt, creosote, and leather.

Joanna Gambetta, Ph.D., wine scientist at University of Newcastle, Australia, found that defoliation at veraison increases sunburn risk; defoliation at end of flowering allows berries to build photoprotective compounds.
Producers in Provence and Napa Valley are abandoning midseason leaf removal and east-side exposure, shifting to late defoliation, kaolin clay sprays, and canopy-focused vineyard design.
At Chêne Bleu in Ventoux, a 40°C heat wave in August 2023 caused significant damage; white varieties now receive no summer leaf removal and Syrah only limited east-side stripping.
Tyrrell's in Hunter Valley reports kaolin clay reduces canopy temperature by up to 9°C; sorting sunburned fruit remains the final defense when prevention fails.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The new releases from Radford Dale, including Elgin and Vinum bottlings from 2025
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I have been following the wines of Radford Dale with some interest over the last three years. The
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Petroné Thomas promoted to winemaker at Radford Dale in 2024, now overseeing both main estate and Elgin wines; she has Burgundy and Beaujolais experience.
Radford Dale Elgin Estate plans varietal bottlings of Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir, Gamay, and Cabernet Franc as vineyard replanting matures.
Cabernet Franc emerged as surprising success at Elgin with only 0.4ha currently planted; two Semillon vineyards being regrapped to Cabernet Franc.
Semillon 2025 from Elgin is final release before vineyard conversion; Grenache 2025 is last bottling including older Stellenbosch Mountain block.
No Frankenstein or Renaissance 2024 releases; fruit redirected to Vinum bottlings as crop lacked required directness for premium range.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 8/9/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Priorat, In Progress
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The new wave is happening in Catalonia's prestige appellation. Plus, 14 bottle recommendations
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jason Wilson
takeaways: Álvaro Palacios L'Ermita 2021, Clos i Terrasses Clos Erasmus 2020, and Familia Nin-Ortiz Mas d'en Cacador 2020 each earned 100-point scores; retail for $1,250, $300, and $180 respectively.
Traditional Priorat reds age 14–18 months in oak, reach 14.5–15.5% ABV, and blend garnacha or carignan with international varieties like syrah or cabernet sauvignon.
Terroir al Límit's Les Manyes uses rare garnacha peluda from 60-year-old vines above 2,600 feet, ages eight months in cement, and contains only 13.5% ABV.

Emerging Priorat producers, Terroir al Límit, Sara Pérez (Mas Martinet), Ferrer Bobet, Josep Grau, Marco Abella, Trossos del Priorat, Hodgkinson, Clos Pachem, Gemma Miró, and Iduvina Olmdeo, represent a shift toward lighter, more complex wines.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Michelin And The Death Of The Wine Guide
NEWSLETTERS.summ: It was entirely predictable that Michelin’s new venture into wine would trigger huffy French recriminations. Its Wine Selection Burgundy 2026, launched this month, awarded nine producers the top accolade of three grapes, another 20 vignerons two grapes, and 33 one grape. A further 32 were merely “selected”.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Michelin's Wine Selection Burgundy 2026 awarded nine producers three grapes, 20 vignerons two grapes, 33 one grape, and 32 were merely selected.
Domaine Arnoux-Lachaux publicly demanded removal from Michelin's guide after receiving only one grape despite being a celebrated Vosne-Romanée house.
Michelin rates producers based on vineyard management and consistency rather than individual wines, unlike competitor Guide Hachette des Vins which rates specific cuvées.
Michelin owns Wine Advocate entirely since 2019 after purchasing 40% in 2017, raising questions about influence on Burgundy selections.
Consumer wine guides emerged in the 1970s-80s but declined as internet access expanded; Michelin's venture marks the definitive end of the print wine guide era.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Six Wines That Stopped Me in My Tracks
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Exceptional new discoveries from Austria, France, Italy and Slovenia
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: A Burgundy-born winemaker named Charly relocated to Lower Austria about a decade ago and produces wines under his own label with a French sensibility.
Charly's Blauer Portugieser 2023, made from grapes sourced from Christoph Hoch, displays ripeness, vivid fruit, and creamy texture atypical of the variety.
Charly owns one hectare of vines and sources additional grapes from friends farming organically or biodynamically.
Three of Charly's wines (Grüner Veltliner 2022, Blaufränkisch 2023, Zweigelt 2023) are available from Gute Weine for €27 per bottle, with EU delivery available.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Notable Releases from Troon Vineyard
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Notes on a Vermentino and two Syrahs, one with some bottle age
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Troon Vineyard released 2025 Vermentino and 2023 Syrah from Oregon's Applegate Valley.
Troon Vineyard, located in Grant's Pass, farms using certified biodynamic and regenerative organic principles.
Troon relies on ambient cultures for fermentation, minimal sulfite at bottling, and ages exclusively in neutral vessels.
Applegate Valley's alluvial soils, Mediterranean sun, and overnight temperature drops from Siskiyou Mountains create ideal ripening conditions.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Q&8 | Wang Yuanzhu Talks Grapes, Grain & Ancient Wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Coram Collective 集岩酿造 ranks among the most intriguing projects to pop up in China in recent years. Founded in 2023, with production from 2024, this
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Coram Collective, founded in 2023 with production from 2024, co-ferments rice wine with grape varieties like Chardonnay and Merlot, and innovates huangjiu (yellow wine).
Co-founder Alex Yuanzhu Wang's huangjiu with aged Chinese tangerine peel emerged from a Christmas Eve 2024 experience in Shaoxing, inspired by citrus and wheat flavor pairing.
Coram's Chardomi (80% Chardonnay, 20% glutinous rice) and Merlot-rice blend are listed in over 100 restaurants and bistros across Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, and Chengdu.
Good huangjiu ages best between three and eight years; most modern styles are fresher and cleaner than older, sweeter, more oxidized versions.
Wang dispels the misconception that huangjiu is cooking wine; premium huangjiu is a traditional fermented beverage meant for drinking with food or socially.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A wine of straw
NEWSLETTERS.summ: "Why all the grape drying?" "For something beautiful my boy!"
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Dessert wine consumption has declined for approximately 75 years, with no expected recovery amid current concerns about sugar and alcohol.
Raül Bobet, co-owner of Ferrer-Bobet in Priorat, Catalunya, released a dessert wine requiring 20 years of aging.
Goût Russe Champagne of the 19th century contained 300g/l of sugar for the Russian market, establishing the historical peak of wine sweetness.
